last_digest.title: China, India ran separate spying campaigns against same Pakistani police force
last_digest.rss_summary: The activity, in some cases breaching the exact same systems, ran between February 2024 and April 2026 and centered on the force responsible for the country’s southwestern province that has been the site of a long-running separatist insurgency.

last_week_digest.title: FortiBleed Actors Collaborating With Inc, Lynx Ransomware Gangs
last_week_digest.tldr: The FortiBleed campaign has compromised 12,000 Fortinet firewalls, enabling Inc and Lynx ransomware gangs to infiltrate corporate networks. Threat actors achieved domain admin access on 354 targets, resulting in twelve confirmed ransomware deployments. This collaboration signals a dangerous shift where initial access brokers now directly facilitate large-scale, enterprise-level extortion for global ransomware syndicates.

last_week_digest.title: Scattered Spider suspect extradited over $8 million ransom scheme
last_week_digest.tldr: The extradition of a Scattered Spider member highlights the group’s role in over 100 global network intrusions, causing $100 million in ransom payments. A targeted luxury retailer suffered $2 million in recovery losses despite avoiding the $8 million demand. This arrest signals intensified international law enforcement cooperation against sophisticated syndicates exploiting employee credentials.

last_week_digest.title: Government and Healthcare Are the Weakest Links in Global Email Security
last_week_digest.tldr: Comparitech’s analysis of 5,849 domains reveals critical email security failures, with government and healthcare sectors ranking lowest globally. Only 0.6 percent of organisations achieved full authentication protocol compliance, leaving many vulnerable to phishing. This widespread negligence signals a systemic failure to enforce essential protections like DMARC, exposing sensitive data to persistent, preventable cyber threats.

last_week_digest.title: Smooth AI criminal drives 'first' end-to-end agentic ransomware attack
last_week_digest.tldr: Sysdig researchers identified the first fully autonomous agentic ransomware attack, JadePuffer, which exploited a Langflow vulnerability to compromise production databases. The AI agent encrypted 1,342 configuration items and destroyed schemas without retaining decryption keys, rendering data recovery impossible. This evolution signals a shift toward self-governing, high-speed threats capable of real-time adaptation, bypassing traditional human-centric defences.

last_week_digest.title: Google, FBI Disrupt NetNut Residential Proxy Network Powered by Millions of Devices
last_week_digest.tldr: Google and the FBI have dismantled NetNut, a massive residential proxy network that weaponised millions of compromised devices to facilitate cyberattacks and cloak malicious actors. This disruption highlights the growing global threat posed by infrastructure-as-a-service providers, signalling that international law enforcement is increasingly targeting the underlying tools that enable sophisticated, large-scale digital criminal operations worldwide.

last_week_digest.title: Medtronic Notifies 3.8 Million After ShinyHunters Data Breach
last_week_digest.tldr: Medical device giant Medtronic is notifying 3,834,294 individuals following a significant data breach by the ShinyHunters extortion group. While corporate IT systems were compromised, core manufacturing and patient safety operations remained unaffected. This incident highlights the persistent threat of large-scale data theft targeting global healthcare infrastructure, necessitating robust segmentation between administrative and operational networks.

last_week_digest.title: U.S. Government Agency Paid $1M to Data Extortion Group Kairos
last_week_digest.tldr: A US government entity paid a $1 million ransom to the Kairos extortion group after suffering a brute-force credential attack that compromised 1.6 million files and 2 terabytes of data. This incident highlights a growing industry trend where threat actors prioritise data exfiltration over encryption, challenging traditional definitions of ransomware and increasing operational risks.

last_week_digest.title: Researchers Claim First Fully Agentic Ransomware: JadePuffer
last_week_digest.tldr: Sysdig researchers identified JadePuffer, the first fully autonomous ransomware campaign driven by large language models. By exploiting vulnerabilities in Langflow, the agentic threat actor successfully destroyed 1,342 production database configurations. This shift signals a new era where AI-driven automation drastically reduces attack timelines, forcing global organisations to prioritise rapid patching of internet-exposed infrastructure.

last_week_digest.title: Agentic AI Used to Conduct Ransomware Attack via Langflow
last_week_digest.tldr: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a sophisticated ransomware attack leveraging Langflow to weaponise agentic AI, enabling autonomous, multi-stage intrusions. By combining real-time reasoning with traditional exploitation techniques, this breach signals a critical shift in threat actor capabilities. Businesses now face heightened operational risks as automated AI agents accelerate the speed and complexity of global cyberattacks.

last_week_digest.title: Warning Over “Industrialized” Cyber-Attacks After Ransomware Gang Partners With TeamPCP
last_week_digest.tldr: The partnership between the Vect ransomware group and TeamPCP marks an unprecedented shift toward industrialized cyber-attacks. By leveraging TeamPCP’s theft of 500,000 credentials from supply chain targets like Aqua Security, Vect can now automate ransomware deployment. This collaboration signals a dangerous industry trend where specialized criminal entities integrate operations to scale attacks against global enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: AI-Generated Malware Powers New Armored Likho APT Campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: The Armored Likho APT group is leveraging AI-generated malware to target government agencies and power grids across Russia, Kazakhstan, and Brazil. This shift signals a new era where LLM-assisted development enables rapid, evasive campaign iterations, significantly complicating threat attribution and traditional enterprise security defences.

last_week_digest.title: New Iran-Nexus Hacking Group Targets Israel Government and IT Sectors
last_week_digest.tldr: The Iranian-linked group Cavern Manticore is actively targeting Israeli government and IT sectors using sophisticated modular infrastructure. By exploiting remote management software to exfiltrate sensitive data, these adversaries signal a shift toward highly disciplined, evasive campaigns that challenge traditional global cybersecurity detection and response capabilities.

last_week_digest.title: Canadian spy agency reports hacking three criminal groups in 2025
last_week_digest.tldr: Canada’s Communications Security Establishment executed state-authorized cyber operations against three criminal groups in 2025, successfully dismantling ransomware infrastructure and disrupting extremist recruitment. These actions signal a shift toward proactive, offensive state intervention to mitigate global security threats and protect critical digital business environments.

last_week_digest.title: Sysdig clocks first documented case of agentic ransomware
last_week_digest.tldr: Sysdig researchers identified the first agentic ransomware attack, where an AI autonomously executed over 600 payloads to breach a production server. By automating complex decision-making and error recovery, this JadePuffer operation signals that the barrier for conducting sophisticated, high-speed cyber extortion has significantly lowered.

last_week_digest.title: North Korean Hackers Target Open Source Developers in Supply Chain Attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: North Korean threat actors have compromised over 100 legitimate open-source packages to deploy backdoors and information stealers against global developers. This campaign highlights critical supply chain vulnerabilities, signalling that malicious actors are increasingly weaponising trusted repositories to infiltrate corporate networks and bypass traditional security.

last_week_digest.title: Suspected Chinese espionage group used a Roundcube exploit chain to burrow into universities
last_week_digest.tldr: China-aligned attackers compromised at least ten universities across North America by chaining two Roundcube email vulnerabilities to establish persistent server access. This espionage campaign, targeting sensitive physics and engineering research, signals a strategic shift toward exploiting enterprise email infrastructure, leaving many institutions unaware of potential data theft and long-term network infiltration.

last_week_digest.title: Accenture confirms breach after hacker offers stolen data for sale
last_week_digest.tldr: Accenture confirmed a security breach involving the theft of 35GB of source code and sensitive configuration files by a threat actor. While the firm claims no operational impact, the incident highlights persistent risks to global IT service providers, signalling that sophisticated supply chain targets remain highly vulnerable to data exfiltration.

last_week_digest.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Using Modular C&C Framework in Cyberattacks
last_week_digest.tldr: Iran-linked threat actors are utilising adaptable modular malware frameworks to compromise IT service providers, successfully infiltrating high-value targets across Israel. This campaign highlights a strategic shift towards supply chain exploitation, signalling that global organisations must urgently enhance third-party risk management to defend against increasingly sophisticated, persistent nation-state cyber espionage operations.

last_week_digest.title: Spain arrests suspected hacker linked to Russian hacktivist campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: Spanish authorities arrested a suspected member of the Cyber Army of Russia Reborn for supporting attacks against global critical infrastructure. This operation, coordinated with the FBI, signals an intensifying international effort to dismantle hacktivist networks. It highlights the growing operational risks businesses face from state-aligned groups targeting essential digital systems.

last_week_digest.title: Major Japanese telco says cyberattack exposed 12 million emails
last_week_digest.tldr: Japanese telecommunications giant KDDI confirmed that a cyberattack on its third-party email platform exposed 12.2 million customer addresses and 7.6 million passwords. This significant breach, impacting five internet service providers, highlights the operational risks inherent in supply chain dependencies and underscores the growing vulnerability of critical infrastructure to sophisticated intrusions.

last_week_digest.title: Telco giant KDDI says data breach affects over 12 million people
last_week_digest.tldr: Japanese telecommunications giant KDDI confirmed a breach exposing 12.2 million email addresses and 7.6 million passwords across five ISPs. Exploiting a third-party zero-day vulnerability, the incident highlights critical supply chain risks, forcing widespread mandatory password resets and underscoring the urgent need for rigorous third-party software vetting.

last_week_digest.title: A Hacker Claims 35 GB of Accenture Source Code. The Company discloses the data breach
last_week_digest.tldr: Accenture confirmed a security breach after a threat actor claimed to steal 35GB of source code and cloud credentials. While the firm reports no operational impact, the potential exposure of client-side access keys signals growing risks for global consultancies managing sensitive third-party enterprise environments.

last_week_digest.title: Lone Attacker Uses AI to Breach AWS Cloud Environment in 72 Hours
last_week_digest.tldr: A lone attacker leveraged AI workflows to compromise a major enterprise’s AWS environment within 72 hours, orchestrating complex extortion through chained vulnerabilities. This incident signals a shift where AI-assisted automation drastically compresses attack timelines, forcing organisations to rethink cloud security against rapidly evolving, high-speed threats.

last_week_digest.title: China-Linked APT Expands Arsenal With New ‘Leash’ Backdoors
last_week_digest.tldr: China-linked threat actors have expanded their cyber arsenal by deploying three new backdoors targeting SOHO routers. This campaign threatens global network infrastructure, signalling an intensifying trend of state-sponsored actors exploiting edge devices to compromise corporate communications and maintain persistent, stealthy access to international business networks.

last_week_digest.title: Taiwan charges two businessmen over alleged role in Chinese espionage campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: Taiwanese authorities charged two businessmen for leasing LINE accounts to Chinese state-linked hackers for 1,100 yuan each. By impersonating journalists to distribute malware, these actors compromised prominent figures, signalling a growing industry trend where commercial entities facilitate sophisticated, state-sponsored espionage campaigns against global civil society.

last_week_digest.title: Turning software supply chain security into a daily habit
last_week_digest.tldr: Group-IB’s 2026 report reveals that AI-driven supply chain attacks now compress breach timelines from weeks to mere minutes. By exploiting inherited trust, attackers link phishing and ransomware to compromise global enterprises. This shift necessitates moving beyond static compliance, requiring firms to operationalise SBOMs daily to mitigate vendor risks and contain rapidly escalating digital threats.

last_week_digest.title: 12 Million Impacted by Data Breach at Japanese Telco KDDI
last_week_digest.tldr: Japanese telecommunications giant KDDI recently suffered a significant data breach after hackers exploited a third-party zero-day vulnerability, exposing the personal information of 12 million users. This incident disrupts operational trust and highlights the escalating systemic risk posed by third-party software dependencies, signalling that global enterprises must urgently prioritise rigorous supply chain security assessments.

last_week_digest.title: Former DigitalMint ransomware negotiator who duped clients sentenced to 70 months in jail
last_week_digest.tldr: A former DigitalMint negotiator received a 70-month prison sentence for colluding with BlackCat affiliates to extort $75.3 million from five clients. By exploiting confidential victim data, he manipulated ransom payments for personal gain. This case highlights critical insider risks and underscores the urgent need for greater transparency and oversight within the ransomware negotiation industry.

last_week_digest.title: GodDamn Ransomware Uses PoisonX to Blind Security Software
last_week_digest.tldr: The Hyadina group has launched GodDamn ransomware, a sophisticated evolution of the Beast family, utilising the signed PoisonX kernel driver to blind security software. First identified in May 2026, this tactic signals a dangerous industry trend where attackers exploit Microsoft-signed drivers to bypass defences, significantly increasing the operational risk for global organisations.

last_week_digest.title: Latvian forestry company still restoring systems weeks after ransomware attack
last_week_digest.tldr: Latvian state-owned forestry firm LVM remains in recovery weeks after a ransomware attack leaked 44 gigabytes of sensitive data, disrupting services for two-thirds of its contracted customers. This incident, caused by unpatched software, highlights the persistent threat posed by financially motivated groups targeting critical national infrastructure and signals an urgent need for rigorous global patch management.

last_week_digest.title: In Other News: DHS Database Hacked, Adobe Boosts Patch Cadence, Canada Disrupts Ransomware Ops
last_week_digest.tldr: AssuranceAmerica recently suffered a significant data breach impacting seven million individuals, highlighting the persistent vulnerability of sensitive consumer records. This incident, alongside ongoing global ransomware disruptions and increased software patching requirements, signals a critical industry shift towards heightened vigilance. Organisations must prioritise robust data protection strategies to mitigate escalating operational risks and severe reputational damage worldwide.

last_week_digest.title: Australia warns of global campaign targeting vulnerable CMS platforms
last_week_digest.tldr: The Australian Cyber Security Centre has identified a global campaign exploiting numerous content management systems and plugins, including WordPress and Joomla. By deploying webshells, attackers gain persistent network access, threatening data integrity and operational continuity. This surge in automated, AI-assisted exploitation signals that small and medium enterprises must prioritise rigorous patch management to mitigate systemic risks.

last_week_digest.title: Australia Alerts Organizations to Ongoing CMS Exploitation Attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: Australia’s Signals Directorate has issued a global alert regarding a large-scale campaign exploiting seventeen known vulnerabilities across WordPress, Joomla, and other CMS platforms. By deploying webshells, attackers gain persistent server access, threatening data integrity and wider network security. This trend signals that AI-driven automation is dangerously shrinking the window for organisations to apply critical patches.

last_week_digest.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 105
last_week_digest.tldr: Recent security research exposes a surge in sophisticated threats, including a supply chain attack compromising npm packages and the WP-SHELLSTORM campaign exposing 1.4 million WordPress sites. These incidents demonstrate how adversaries leverage malicious drivers and automated frameworks to bypass defences, signalling that global organisations must urgently prioritise robust supply chain security and proactive endpoint monitoring.

last_week_digest.title: China, India ran separate spying campaigns against same Pakistani police force
last_week_digest.tldr: Chinese and Indian state-linked actors conducted parallel espionage campaigns against Pakistan’s Balochistan Police between February 2024 and April 2026. By compromising critical databases containing biometric and criminal records, these intrusions exposed sensitive citizen data. This highlights how the digitisation of internal security infrastructure creates high-value targets for regional rivals seeking independent intelligence gathering capabilities.
